subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared async resource lifecycle primitive for retry, plugin/channel cleanup, gateway shutdown, and delivery drains, and where should that ownership boundary live?
rationale: Current main has targeted fixes but no shared primitive; adding one would create a cross-boundary lifecycle API and possibly plugin SDK contract that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and define the minimal owner boundary, API shape, and proof matrix before implementation.

options.title: Continue targeted fixes only
options.body: Close or narrow this tracker if maintainers decide the existing per-surface guards are the desired architecture.

options.title: Plugin SDK lifecycle extension
options.body: Route the remaining work to a plugin/channel-owned lifecycle API if the goal is mainly external plugin resource cleanup rather than embedded runner or gateway state.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define the minimal owner boundary, API shape, and proof matrix before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to recent adjacent work on channel lifecycle, session reset, and delivery queue design, making this the strongest available owner signal for the cross-boundary decision.
